findings.title: Removing the lock around BuildIndex introduces a TOCTOU race for concurrent builds of the same key
findings.body: The original code held `cacheMu.Lock()` for the entire `BuildIndex` call, which prevented two goroutines from building the same index concurrently. The new code only locks when writing to the cache at the end. This means two concurrent callers of `getOrCreateIndex` (in search.go) can both observe a nil index from `GetIndex`, both invoke `BuildIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource`, and both fully build the index. The second write to `b.cache[key]` silently overwrites the first, orphaning the first index. This wastes resources and can produce subtle inconsistencies if the two builds observe slightly different data. A per-key synchronization mechanism (e.g., `golang.org/x/sync/singleflight`) would preserve the concurrency improvement across different keys while preventing duplicate builds for the same key.

findings.title: Init failure in NewResourceServer leaks the cancel function and any partially-initialized resources
findings.body: When `s.Init(ctx)` fails at line 258, `NewResourceServer` returns an error without calling `cancel()` (the context cancel func created at line 229). This leaks the context and any goroutines or resources tied to it. Additionally, if `newSearchSupport` succeeded (allocating a builder cache, etc.) but `Init` subsequently fails, those resources are never cleaned up. The `cancel()` should be called (or deferred with a success check) before returning the error.

findings.title: Data race on totalBatchesIndexed incremented from multiple errgroup goroutines without synchronization
findings.body: The variable `totalBatchesIndexed` is a plain `int` that is incremented (`totalBatchesIndexed++`) inside `group.Go` closures that run concurrently (up to `s.initWorkers` goroutines). This is a data race under the Go memory model. While this is pre-existing code, the PR's change to propagate `ctx` through this function makes it a good opportunity to fix. Use `atomic.Int64` or collect results from the errgroup instead.

findings.title: History and Origin methods will panic with nil pointer dereference when search is not configured
findings.body: If `opts.Search.Resources` is nil in `ResourceServerOptions`, `s.search` remains nil. The `Search` method correctly checks for this (`if s.search == nil`), but `History` (line 924) and `Origin` (line 929) call `s.search.History(...)` and `s.search.Origin(...)` without a nil check, which will panic. Previously the `s.Init(ctx)` call was present (though it also wouldn't have prevented this), but now that these are the only guards removed, the nil dereference is the immediate failure mode for any deployment without search configured.
